Douglas Service GmbHWithin Architecture & Application Portfolio Management, you shape the evolution of our Enterprise Architecture at Group level. At the core is the development of an effective Enterprise Architecture Management (EAM) practice in LeanIX — as the foundation for reliable transparency across business processes, applications, data and technologies.How do you make sure your architecture expertise doesn't stay conceptual, but leads to target pictures and solution options that genuinely work in everyday business? A team driving architecture across domain boundaries is looking forward to supporting well-founded decisions and advancing our IT landscape together with you.TASKS WITH IMPACT- You build up Enterprise Architecture Management and LeanIX as the central architecture repository, establish it, and continuously develop the metamodel, fact sheets, roles and governance processes further.- You create transparency across the IT landscape by structuring, documenting and making usable business processes, business capabilities, applications, data, technologies, interfaces and dependencies.- You establish data quality standards and clear responsibilities, actively address data gaps, and position LeanIX as a reliable basis for decision-making in day-to-day business.- You drive stakeholder enablement together with business functions and IT, run trainings, roadshows and reviews, and embed architecture processes sustainably into everyday work.- You accompany selected architecture topics and business domains independently — from analysing the current landscape to developing target pictures, evaluating options, and preparing architecture sketches and impact assessments for business functions and IT.- You further develop reusable architecture principles, standards and guardrails, and identify potential for standardisation and rationalisation.- You assess new requirements and technologies for their impact on the enterprise architecture, prioritise them, and translate them into concrete architecture measures.YOUR SKILLS- You bring several years of experience in enterprise architecture and complex IT landscapes.- Very good practical knowledge of LeanIX or comparable EAM tools, together with experience in target architectures, portfolio management and transformation processes, sets you apart; experience in a retail environment is a plus.- Strategic thinking allows you to translate the overall architecture into clear target pictures and development options.- Structured, traceable documentation of complex interrelations in LeanIX is a natural part of your way of working.- Building sustainable relationships with business departments and IT is part of your day-to-day work, and you actively foster exchange within the architecture community.- In daily operations, you embed architecture processes in a hands-on way and ensure they are used sustainably.- Driving the ongoing development of the IT landscape, you identify synergies as well as standardization and rationalization potential.- Whether with internal or international stakeholders, you communicate confidently in English and German in a business context.

jobs.description: PhD Position (m/f/d)(Entgeltgruppe: EG 13 TV-L)Einsatzbereich: Institute of Medical Microbiology - AG KnuschkeStellen ID: 14047Eintritt: 01.01.2027Umfang: Teilzeit / 25,025 Std.Vertragsart: BefristetBefristung: 36 Monate ab BesetzungIhre Aufgaben: About the ProjectWe are offering a fully funded PhD position supported by the German Research Foundation (DFG) to investigate the antiviral role of hemoglobin during influenza A virus infection.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral activity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.Your Tasks- Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) functions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cells- Apply molecular biology techniques- Plan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studies- Present research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publications- Assist in supervising Bachelor's/Master's studentsIhr Profil: - You have a university degree (Master or Diploma) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related field- Solid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniques- Experience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantage- Strong interest in basic research in virology/immunology- Independent, structured, and team-oriented working style- Excellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredFreuen Sie sich auf: - An exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research field- Dedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminars- State-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital Essen- Enrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Science ‘BIOME’ (https://www.uni-due.de/biome (https://www.uni-due.de/biome) )- Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 years- A collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideas- Einen sicheren Arbeitsplatz im öffentlichen Dienst des Landes NRW- Faire Bezahlung nach Tarif (TV-L) inkl. We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Fellow in Computational Cancer Evolution (f/m/x)Department I of Internal Medicine - CECADYour tasksWe are looking for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a proven track record in computational cancer evolution to join our Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory at the CECAD Research Center in Cologne. In this role, you will reconstruct the clonal and subclonal architecture of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and track its evolution under targeted therapies. Using bulk and single-cell sequencing data, you will infer tumour phylogenies and quantify intratumour heterogeneity, subclonal selection and genomic instability (e.g. copy-number alterations, whole-genome doubling and chromothripsis).You will identify evolutionary trajectories leading to treatment resistance, relapse and Richter transformation. Furthermore, you will develop and apply computational methods based on evolutionary principles and integrate genomic, transcriptomic and spatial data with clinical outcomes. Your analyses will link evolutionary features to treatment response, MRD kinetics and survival.For this work, the lab has access to blood and bone marrow samples from more than 900 patients with CLL treated within prospective clinical trials of the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), including samples taken before treatment and at relapse, linked to detailed clinical and measurable residual disease (MRD) data.You will lead your own projects, contribute to collaborative projects within the lab and with external partners, and co-supervise PhD and Master students.Your profile• A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics, physics, computer science or a related field• A proven track record in computational cancer evolution, demonstrated by first-author publications• Hands-on experience in reconstructing clonal and subclonal tumour evolution from sequencing data (e.g. clonal deconvolution, phylogenetic inference, mutational signatures)• Experience in copy-number and structural variant analysis from whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing data; experience with single-cell DNA or RNA sequencing data is a plus• Fluency in Python and/or R, and experience with reproducible workflows (e.g. Snakemake, Nextflow) on high performance computing clusters• Experience with longitudinal or clinical trial data and with haematological malignancies is a plus• Ability to work independently and in close collaboration with clinicians and wet-lab scientists• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spokenOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future in detailThe Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory (www.al-sawaf-lab.com), led by Prof Othman Al-Sawaf and based at the CECAD and Department I of Internal Medicine, was founded in 2024 and is funded by a large Emmy-Noether-Grant of the German Research Council (DFG). The focus of the lab is to integrate multimodal analyses to study the plasticity, evolution and prognosis of cancer with a special focus on hematological malignancies. environmentAbout the TeamOur Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid.
